text:
Joel: heads-up — noticed a small but visible duplicate-billing spike for streaming resumes during a regional NAT switchover. clients reconnect, resume succeeds, but token attribution flips route and both routes get charged for ~30s.
Anya: can you paste the console trace / logs? curious whether resume id matched the original route or if we issued a fresh session.
Joel: pasting minimal logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-21T14:05:12Z INFO resume accepted session_id=aa12 route=eu-west-1-azb resume_token=rt:abc123
2026-03-21T14:05:13Z WARN route-change detected client_ip=34.56.78.90 old_route=eu-west-1-azb new_route=eu-west-1-bzc
2026-03-21T14:05:14Z INFO resume replay started session_id=aa12 route=eu-west-1-bzc resume_token=rt:abc123
2026-03-21T14:05:42Z BILLING charge route=eu-west-1-azb session_id=aa12 tokens=120
2026-03-21T14:05:43Z BILLING charge route=eu-west-1-bzc session_id=aa12 tokens=20
```
Anya: ugh. so resume_token was valid across routes (we don't bind token to route currently). resume accepted on new route, but old route still billed for stale in-flight replay.
Michael: that's consistent with the ticket we saw last month. I think the core issue is resume-path idempotency + incomplete session handoff. two overlapping workers both believe they're owner for short window.
Maya: is this an edge of our lease-transfer window? we have a 30s tombstone on old worker before it stops billing, right?
Joel: yes — tombstone is 30s. NAT change caused client to immediately land on new route; new route accepted resume and started replay. old route still had buffered events to bill. net effect: same session billed twice.
Anya: proposals: (1) include route_id/epoch in resume_tokens so new route can refuse resume if token indicates different affinity unless a forced-claim flag is present. (2) emit a resume_route_mismatch metric and console alert. (3) server side: when accepting resume on new route, signal old route to revoke billing window immediately if possible.
Michael: +1. Another idea: central resume coordinator (cheap state in control plane) to serialise resume handoffs for a few seconds to prevent duplicate billing. downside: control plane hop.
Maya: for immediate mitigation, can we change tombstone behavior: if resume accepted elsewhere with same session_id, old route should drop billing and mark as handed-off. need a cross-route pubsub message (we already have route-control topic).
Joel: quick patch we tested in canary: new-route publishes `route.claimed` with {session_id, new_route, resume_nonce}, old-route watches and if session_id matches and resume_nonce differs it stops billing and drains without charging. reduced duplicates in canary by ~98%. logs looked like: 
```
[route.claimed] session=aa12 new=eu-west-1-bzc nonce=42
old-route: heard claim -> stop billing for session aa12 (grace-0s)
```
Anya: that sounds promising. What telemetry do we need to expose in console so SRE / support can quickly identify affected customers?
Maya: add per-session tags: route_history (last 3 routes), resume_nonce, resume_origin_ts. expose `resume_route_mismatch_count` and a per-tenant `duplicate_resume_billing` gauge. also add a small per-session timeline view in Console that shows route handoffs and billing windows.
Michael: UX note: console alerting should default to sampling (we don't want noisy alerts). show top affected customers, then let ops deep-dive. also provide an auto-annotated repro link that opens a trace in Console with the claim events highlighted.
deploy-bot: canary rollout for route.claimed revocation patch -> 10% eu-west -> started at 2026-03-21T16:00:00Z. monitor: resume_route_mismatch, duplicate_resume_billing.
ops-bot: alert fired at 2026-03-21T16:07:21Z: duplicate_resume_billing > threshold in eu-west. lookincount=12.
Joel: we should make the resume token schema change a short RFC. sketches: add fields `route_id`, `session_epoch` and optional `force_claim` flag. When new route sees token.route_id != self.route_id and force_claim==false -> either reject resume (401 resume-required) or publish route.claimed and wait for confirmation from old route (500–1000ms window).
Anya: for backward compat, servers should accept tokens w/o route_id (old tokens) but mark them as legacy and emit telemetry. we'll need migration: mint tokens with current route_id for new sessions, and rotate tokens on significant restarts.
Maya: implement console change as a beta flag initially. we can add `Session Timeline` in the session detail panel with an icon for route claim events and billing ticks.
Michael: who picks up the RFC and console PR? I can do the resume token RFC text. Joel + Anya: will pair on server implementation PR. Maya: can you do the Console UI issue?
Joel: assigned work item created: RFC#4921 (resume-token-route-affinity) -> assignees: Michael, Joel. Server PR branch: `fix/route-claiming-2026` (Anya + Joel). Console ticket: UI-1107 (Maya).
Anya: quick follow-up question — does anyone see a compatibility problem with function-calling or webhook-forwarding that expects session_id to be sticky?
Michael: only if downstream assumes single-route monotonic token counts. we'll add a small migration note in the RFC.
Maya: timeline: canary 10% now -> if metrics drop to <1% duplicate, promote. target full deploy in 48h.
Joel: thanks all. I'll dump the canary traces and a short repro script in the ticket. cc @SRE if you want to tweak alert thresholds. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: note: follow-up alerting rule created: `duplicate_resume_billing` -> notify #eng-oncall and page at P2 if sustained > 5m.
